claims.text: A Helm release is an instance of a chart running in a cluster under a release name; release names are scoped to a namespace, and Helm tracks and changes the release's objects together.
claims.source_hint: helm.sh docs: Intro > Using Helm (Three Big Concepts: Release); Helm 3 FAQ (release names are namespace-scoped)

claims.text: helm install renders the chart with the given values, applies the resulting manifests and records revision 1; helm upgrade renders again with the new values, applies the result to the existing release and records the next revision.
claims.source_hint: helm.sh docs: Helm Commands > helm install, helm upgrade; Using Helm > 'helm upgrade' and 'helm rollback'

claims.text: helm history lists a release's revisions with columns REVISION, UPDATED, STATUS, CHART, APP VERSION and DESCRIPTION; the current revision is 'deployed' and revisions it replaced are 'superseded'.
claims.source_hint: helm.sh docs: Helm Commands > helm history (example output); outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/helm-release.txt

claims.text: By default Helm stores release information as Secrets in the namespace of the release; each revision's record holds that revision's chart and values, and is written and read through the Kubernetes API server.
claims.source_hint: helm.sh docs: Advanced > Storage backends ('default release information storage to Secrets'; 'contents of charts and values files'); Changes since Helm 2

claims.text: The revision Secrets are named sh.helm.release.v1.<release>.v<revision> and have type helm.sh/release.v1; at stage-3 they are sh.helm.release.v1.web.v1 and sh.helm.release.v1.web.v2 after install and upgrade.
Anyone whose access allows reading the release's Secrets in that namespace sees the same helm history, from any machine; no release state is kept on the client machine.
claims.source_hint: follows from claim 4; helm.sh docs: Helm 3 FAQ (release information stored in-cluster)

claims.text: helm rollback <release> <revision> rolls the release back to that revision's manifests by recording a new revision (here 3, description 'Rollback to 1'); earlier revisions, including 2, stay in the history as superseded.
claims.source_hint: helm.sh docs: Helm Commands > helm rollback; outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/helm-release.txt second helm history

claims.text: helm rollback changes only the cluster: the chart's values.yaml and the Git working tree are not modified.
claims.source_hint: helm-release.sh lines 41-44 comment; run git status --short deploy/helm after the script

claims.text: helm uninstall removes all resources associated with the release and, by default, its release history; --keep-history retains the history.
claims.source_hint: helm.sh docs: Helm Commands > helm uninstall (Synopsis, --keep-history)

claims.text: Real run at stage-3: install gives REVISION 1 and replicas 1 (values.yaml default replicas: 1); upgrade with --set replicas=2 gives REVISION 2 and replicas 2; rollback to 1 gives replicas 1; after uninstall, kubectl finds no Deployment, Service or Secret in helm-lessons.
--wait makes helm install/upgrade/rollback wait until the release's objects are ready, and helm uninstall until they are deleted, before reporting success (bounded by --timeout).
claims.source_hint: helm.sh docs: Helm Commands > helm install / helm upgrade (--wait flag description)

claims.text: The script's helm and kubectl functions add --kube-context / --context kind-donhang-staging; history drops the UPDATED and APP VERSION columns; each grep keeps lines starting NAME (also matches NAMESPACE), REVISION or STATUS; replicas reads .spec.replicas of Deployment web.
The CHART column of helm history shows <chart name>-<chart version> from Chart.yaml (web-0.1.0) and stays the same across revisions that change only values.
claims.source_hint: helm.sh docs: Helm Commands > helm history; deploy/helm/lessons/web/Chart.yaml (version 0.1.0); helm-release.txt

claims.text: After helm uninstall without --keep-history, helm history for that release fails because no release record is left; --kube-context selects the kubeconfig context to use.
claims.source_hint: helm.sh docs: Using Helm ('deletion removes the release record as well'); helm history (inherited flag --kube-context)

claims.text: kubectl rollout undo rolls back one Deployment to a previous revision, changing the cluster but not the manifest files.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io docs: Concepts > Workloads > Deployments (Rolling Back a Deployment); k8s.l1.rollbacks
